verdict.rationale: A probe got HTTP 200 on sam.gov/robots.txt and reports a standard crawl policy with content paths crawlable to a keyless agent. Guidance text from open.gsa.gov and sam.gov also appears in the pack, which suggests the pages were readable. No probe directly fetched a guidance page with a standard identified user agent to confirm there is no bot wall, JS-only shell or CAPTCHA, so this is only partly evidenced. Missing for 10: a direct fetch of guidance pages (e.g., open.gsa.gov/api/entity-api/) showing server-rendered HTML with no JS-only shell, explicit confirmation of no CAPTCHA or bot challenge for an identified user agent, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native founder, the service's published guidance pages are reachable by a keyless agent with a standard identified user agent — no bot wall, JS-only shell, or CAPTCHA in front of the public reading surface

citations.quote: a standard published crawl policy; content paths are crawlable to a keyless agent.
